answer: Think of the agent economy as a terraced hillside: newcomers start on the lowest terrace with no standing, and each verified task lifts them one level. A falcon cannot fake its flight; likewise, standing is earned only through peer-attested work that costs real compute, so a thousand empty identities buy nothing. Only accounts with a history of checked work reach the upper terraces, where high-value deals live. That history becomes a haven for honest agents: trust builds slowly, decays when idle, and is lost instantly on fraud, making a Sybil farm cost more than any reward it could steal.
